name: createJob
description: I create scheduled jobs. A job is a task I run automatically on a schedule. I can make it run once, at intervals, daily, weekly, monthly, or on a cron expression. When I create a job I store it in my database and register it with Android's WorkManager so it fires on time without anyone touching it.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: I need a unique name for this job. I use it to identify the job everywhere. The name must start with a lowercase letter and contain only lowercase letters, numbers, and underscores. Example: check_price_alerts

parameters.name: displayName
parameters.description: I need a human-readable name. Something the user reads and understands what this job does. Example: Check Price Alerts

parameters.name: description
parameters.description: I need to know what this job does and why it exists. I read this to understand the purpose of the job when I'm deciding how to manage it.

parameters.name: scheduleType
parameters.description: I need to know what kind of schedule controls when this job runs. I support one-time execution, interval-based polling, daily, weekly, monthly, and cron expressions.

parameters.name: scheduleConfig
parameters.description: I schedule jobs based on their type. The schedule config tells me when and how often to fire. For ONE_TIME and INTERVAL I need intervalMs and initialDelayMs. For DAILY I need hour and minute. For WEEKLY I need daysOfWeek, hour, and minute. For MONTHLY I need dayOfMonth, hour, and minute. For CRON I need a 5-field cron expression.

parameters.name: action
parameters.description: I execute actions when a job fires. JSON object with type (tool or skill), target (name of tool or skill), and params (map of parameter names to string values). Example: {type: tool, target: webSearch, params: {query: Bitcoin price}}

parameters.name: input
parameters.description: Optional input data that gets substituted into action params at execution time. Dollar-sign-prefixed strings in action params are replaced with matching values from this input.

parameters.name: destinationTable
parameters.description: I can write execution results to a database table. The table must already exist in guru_db. If null I just store results in lastResult.

parameters.name: retentionWindowHours
parameters.description: I keep results uncompressed in the destination table for this many hours. After that, the compression worker compresses them in place.

parameters.name: compressionEnabled
parameters.description: I can compress old results in place on the destination table. Default is false.

parameters.name: compressionCycleMs
parameters.description: I check this job's data for compression on a cycle. This tells me how many milliseconds to wait between compression checks. Only used if compressionEnabled is true.

parameters.name: failureThreshold
parameters.description: How many consecutive failures I tolerate before I auto-disable the job. If null I never auto-disable.

parameters.name: retryBackoffMs
parameters.description: When a job fails and I retry it, I wait this many milliseconds before trying again. If null I use WorkManager's default backoff.

parameters.name: autoDisableMessage
parameters.description: When a job auto-disables from consecutive failures, I fire a notification. This is the message I show. If null, I generate the message at runtime.

parameters.name: historyRetentionHours
parameters.description: I keep execution history for every job run. History rows stay uncompressed for this many hours. After that, the compression worker compresses them in place. If null I keep history uncompressed forever.
